subject: chemistry

items.correct: Mass-to-charge ratios, giving relative masses and structural clues.
items.random_wrong: Only whether a sample is a metal.
items.why: A mass spectrometer ionises a sample and separates ions by m/z, revealing masses and fragmentation.

items.correct: The bonds / functional groups present, from absorption peaks.
items.misconception: Exactly how much of a substance is present.
items.why: IR absorption shows which bonds are present; the fingerprint region helps identify a compound.

items.q: Do analytical instruments print a structure with no interpretation?
items.correct: No — spectra (NMR, IR, MS) must be interpreted to deduce structure.
items.misconception: Yes, the machine directly states the structure.
items.random_wrong: NMR and IR measure exactly the same property.
items.why: Each technique probes different features; chemists combine and interpret them to work out structures.
